description:
Assemblyman Croll is a back-bench politician with a florid manner, an unfashionable conscience, and a problem he would like handled before it's a matter of record.

Wire jackals are getting into the Registry overflow. That's the problem he'll say out loud.

The problem he won't say out loud is that the overflow archives were supposed to have been moved eight years ago, that he signed the paper saying they had been, and that he genuinely believed it at the time, which he has discovered isn't a defence anybody accepts.

"Quietly," he says. "It's boring, and boring things become scandals purely by being written down."
name: A Matter of Record

objectives.desc: Cull 4 wire jackals in the buffer wastes west of the quarter
emotes: {who} works the buffer wastes where the archive boxes have gone soft in the weather.
{who} puts down a wire jackal that was dragging a box of somebody's tax history.
{who} kills quietly, which the Assemblyman will later describe as discretion and mean as deniability.
